dimensions.assessment: State, local, and Tribal governments making requests to the United States Postal Service are directly affected.
dimensions.evidence: consider entering into an agreement with an agency of a State government, local government, or Tribal government

dimensions.assessment: The changes alter postal operational boundaries based on local requests, which is administrative in nature.
dimensions.evidence: modify a ZIP code for an area subject to their jurisdiction by-- (A) amending or altering existing ZIP code boundaries; or (B) establishing new ZIP codes.

dimensions.assessment: The pilot program permits the Postal Service to receive money, property, or services from non-federal governments to defray net costs.
dimensions.evidence: receive money, property, or services to defray part or all of the net costs

dimensions.assessment: Requires the Postal Service to establish a new administrative process, designate points of contact, and set up an appeals and cost-defraying pilot program.
dimensions.evidence: establish and make public an administrative process for considering State, local, and Tribal government requests

dimensions.assessment: The pilot program includes a specific termination date of seven years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The pilot program established under this section shall terminate on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment

missing_information: Exact figures on the expected number of ZIP code requests or total financial volume.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a pilot program and administrative process for State, local, and Tribal governments to request and potentially fund ZIP code boundary changes, creating reporting and appeal requirements over a 7-year pilot duration.
